Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zucrypt (development version)

R interface

  • crypt_rand_bytes(n = 1) returns n bytes from the operating system’s cryptographic random source, mirroring openssl::rand_bytes() (#9). R’s random number generator is never used or disturbed, so set.seed() has no effect on it. A failure of the source raises the new zucrypt_entropy_error class and never returns bytes.

  • crypt_aes_gcm_encrypt() and crypt_aes_gcm_decrypt() provide AES-GCM authenticated encryption (#10), with a 12-byte nonce, a 16-byte tag and optional associated data. The nonce is random unless supplied, and the nonce and tag travel as attributes of the ciphertext. Decryption checks the tag first: any alteration, a truncated tag or a wrong key raises the new zucrypt_auth_error class and returns no plaintext. The names and argument order follow openssl, and the ciphertext bytes match, but openssl returns no tag and does not authenticate, so this is a documented difference rather than a mirror.

  • crypt_pbkdf2() derives a key from a raw password with PBKDF2-HMAC over SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512 (#12).

  • RSA, in the openssl-style layer (#80): crypt_read_key(), crypt_read_pubkey(), crypt_write_pem(), crypt_write_der(), crypt_write_pkcs1(), crypt_rsa_keygen(), crypt_signature_create(), crypt_signature_verify(), crypt_rsa_encrypt() and crypt_rsa_decrypt() keep openssl’s names and arguments. Keys are read and written as PKCS#1, PKCS#8 and SubjectPublicKeyInfo, PEM or DER, byte for byte as openssl writes them. Additions: pss = TRUE for RSASSA-PSS, oaep_hash for OAEP over SHA-256 and longer digests, and crypt_rsa_key() and as.list() to build a key from its integers and take it apart. Moduli of 1024 to 4096 bits. A signature that does not verify, or a ciphertext that does not decrypt, is zucrypt_auth_error.

  • Elliptic curves (#81): crypt_ec_keygen(), crypt_ec_dh(), crypt_x25519_keygen(), crypt_x25519_diffie_hellman(), crypt_read_x25519_key(), crypt_read_x25519_pubkey(), crypt_ecdsa_parse() and crypt_ecdsa_write() keep openssl’s names and arguments, and crypt_signature_create() and _verify() sign with ECDSA on P-256, P-384 and P-521, in DER, with deterministic = TRUE for RFC

    1. crypt_ec_key() and as.list() build an EC key from its coordinates and take it apart. EC and X25519 keys are read and written in every encoding openssl uses, byte for byte. Points off the curve, peers on another curve and all-zero X25519 secrets are refused. There is no Ed25519.

  • crypt_sha1(), crypt_sha256(), crypt_sha384() and crypt_sha512() mirror openssl’s digest and HMAC functions on raw input, so that hash = crypt_sha256 works as openssl’s hash = sha256 does.

C interface

  • zuc_random_bytes() is added to the archive, and random_bytes is appended to the registered table; test for it with ZUCRYPT_API_HAS(api, random_bytes). Both are additions, as ABI 1 allows.
  • ZUC_ERR_ENTROPY = 10 is appended to zuc_status.
  • zuc_aead_encrypt(), zuc_aead_decrypt() and zuc_pbkdf2_hmac() are added to the archive, and aead_encrypt, aead_decrypt and pbkdf2_hmac are appended to the table. ZUC_ALG_AES_GCM = 96 is the first identifier in the cipher range, and ZUC_ERR_AUTH = 11 is appended to zuc_status. The digest and HMAC functions refuse ZUC_ALG_AES_GCM.
  • RSA: an opaque zuc_pkey handle with zuc_pkey_parse(), zuc_pkey_generate(), zuc_pkey_public(), zuc_pkey_free(), zuc_pkey_type(), zuc_pkey_bits(), zuc_pkey_is_private(), zuc_pkey_write(), zuc_pkey_sign_hash(), zuc_pkey_verify_hash(), zuc_pkey_encrypt() and zuc_pkey_decrypt(), appended to the archive and the table. New zuc_alg values: ZUC_ALG_RSA_OAEP = 97, ZUC_ALG_RSA_PKCS1V15_CRYPT = 98, ZUC_ALG_RSA = 192, ZUC_ALG_RSA_PKCS1V15_SIGN = 224 and ZUC_ALG_RSA_PSS = 225.
  • Elliptic curves: zuc_pkey_import(), zuc_pkey_export() (the backend’s raw key forms) and zuc_pkey_agree() (ECDH and X25519), appended to the archive and the table; the zuc_pkey_* functions take EC keys too. New zuc_alg values: ZUC_ALG_EC_P256 to _P521 (193-195), ZUC_ALG_X25519 = 196, ZUC_ALG_ECDH = 197, ZUC_ALG_ECDSA = 226 and ZUC_ALG_ECDSA_DETERMINISTIC = 227.

Bug fixes

  • A failing operating-system random source is reported as zucrypt_entropy_error (ZUC_ERR_ENTROPY in C) by every key operation (#140). crypt_rsa_decrypt() reported it as zucrypt_auth_error, as if the ciphertext had been forged, crypt_ec_dh() and crypt_x25519_diffie_hellman() as zucrypt_invalid_argument, as if the peer key were bad, and in C, writing the public half of a private EC or X25519 key as SubjectPublicKeyInfo returned ZUC_ERR_BACKEND. Decryption still reports every padding failure as the one status.

  • In the C API, zuc_aead_encrypt() and zuc_aead_decrypt() now refuse, with ZUC_ERR_OVERLAP, a tag or output buffer that overlaps any other buffer of the call, as zucrypt.h promised (#138). Before, a tag inside the ciphertext silently overwrote it, an output over the tag failed a valid message, and a short tag with partially overlapping input and output zeroed part of the caller’s ciphertext. The R functions were not affected: they never share buffers.

  • crypt_signature_create() and crypt_signature_verify() given a non-blocking connection whose data had not all arrived signed or verified the part received so far, as if it were the whole (#145). Every function that reads a connection (crypt_hash(), crypt_hmac(), crypt_read_key(), crypt_read_pubkey(), and the signature functions’ data and sig) now goes through one reader, which refuses such a connection with zucrypt_connection_error, refuses a text-mode one with zucrypt_invalid_argument, and reports a connection or file that cannot be opened, or a directory given as a key path, as a zucrypt condition rather than R’s own error. A key file is read to its end rather than to the size it had when the read began.

  • crypt_equal() and the AES-CBC functions read past the end of a buffer when given a classed raw vector whose length() method misreports its length: crypt_equal() could answer TRUE wrongly or crash R, and a 1-byte IV was read as 16 (#106). The native code now checks every length, number, name and flag it relies on, rather than trusting R’s checks; a logical NA reaching it is an error rather than FALSE (#107).

  • crypt_ecdsa_parse() reads strict DER (#91). It accepted a SEQUENCE or INTEGER whose length ran past the input, padding a truncated INTEGER with invented zero bytes, and negative and non-minimal INTEGERs. It now refuses them, and bytes after the signature too, which openssl::ecdsa_parse() ignores. Signature verification was not affected.

  • An RSA key over 4096 bits, the bundled library’s limit, is zucrypt_unsupported_algorithm from both crypt_read_key() and crypt_read_pubkey(), in every encoding, and the message names the limit (#93). A public key was reported as “not a key”, and a private key in DER depended on its encoding.

  • C interface: a zuc_hash, zuc_hmac or zuc_aes handle kept across the last zuc_shutdown() returns ZUC_ERR_NOT_READY after a later zuc_init(), and its free leaves the key store alone (#92). Before, the new backend could give its key id to a new handle, and the old handle then encrypted under the new handle’s key, returning ZUC_OK, and its free destroyed that key.

  • C interface: a digest or HMAC update that fails in the backend ends the operation until reset, as a finish does (#108). The handle had stayed “active”, and an empty update on it reported success.

  • C interface: zuc_aead_decrypt() zeroes the output on every ZUC_ERR_AUTH, including a tag of the wrong length, which is refused before the backend runs and used to leave the buffer as it was. Found by the new GCM fuzz target’s oracle.

Backend

  • PSA_WANT_ALG_GCM and PSA_WANT_ALG_PBKDF2_HMAC are enabled. Re-deriving the trim added two upstream sources, gcm.c and psa_crypto_aead.c, and no header: 115 vendored files. Measured on macOS x86-64, the source tarball grew from 548 KB to 580 KB, zucrypt.so from 162 KB to 188 KB, and libzucrypt.a from 518 KB to 632 KB.
  • RSA and the PK, PEM, ASN.1 and Base64 modules are enabled. The trim adds 15 upstream sources and 14 headers: 144 vendored files, 37 compiled. Measured on macOS x86-64, the source tarball grew to 730 KB, zucrypt.so to 536 KB and libzucrypt.a to 1.3 MB.
  • The NIST curves, Curve25519, ECDSA (with RFC 6979) and ECDH are enabled: 6 more upstream sources and 3 headers, 153 vendored files, 43 compiled. The source tarball is 854 KB, zucrypt.so 656 KB and libzucrypt.a 1.6 MB on macOS x86-64. tools/make-ec-kat.py extracts the RFC 6979, RFC 7748, RFC 5903 and RFC 7515 vectors and checks them against Python’s cryptography. The allocation sweep’s window holds deterministic ECDSA and X25519, about 10,000 of its 13,000 positions.
  • The backend allocates through zuc_int_calloc(), which records a failed allocation. The RSA functions report any failure that followed one as ZUC_ERR_MEMORY: inside bignum and ASN.1 code an allocation failure otherwise surfaced as an invalid key, a bad argument or an RNG failure.
  • tools/make-rsa-kat.py extracts the RFC 7515 A.2 and RFC 7516 A.1 and A.2 vectors and generates PSS and OAEP ones, and checks them all against Python’s cryptography; the tests cross-verify with openssl 2.4.2.
  • The AEAD and KDF vectors are checked outside the package by tools/check-kat.py, against Python’s cryptography and hashlib, and tools/make-kat.R --check compares the GCM ciphertexts with openssl.
  • On glibc, a getrandom() call interrupted by a signal is retried instead of being reported as an entropy failure.

zucrypt 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-10-23

First release, and the first on CRAN. A focused set of cryptographic primitives over raw vectors, backed by a vendored, pinned crypto library, published to R and to C. The seven R functions are stable, and the static archive is frozen as ABI 1, after its first consumer – zuxlsx’s decryption of password-protected workbooks – was built and tested against it. The registered table is experimental (see “C interface” below).

R interface

Seven functions, and deliberately no more:

  • crypt_hash() and crypt_hmac() — SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 digests and keyed digests, of a raw vector or of everything a connection yields: crypt_hash(file(path)) hashes a file in 1 MiB chunks without reading it into memory (#11). Raw vectors in, raw vectors out; a character value is never given a guessed encoding and never treated as a file name. Algorithm names match exactly, with no partial matching and no fallback.
  • crypt_hex() — lower-case hex of a raw vector, converted in C, for printing or storing a digest. Hex stays an explicit step at the call site (#59).
  • crypt_equal() — constant-time comparison. Unequal lengths return FALSE rather than pretending the length is secret.
  • crypt_aes_cbc_encrypt_nopad() and crypt_aes_cbc_decrypt_nopad() — AES-128/192/256 in CBC mode, with no padding and no authentication. Interoperability tools for formats that specify unauthenticated CBC, not a way to encrypt something of your own.
  • crypt_info() — what this build contains, read from the compiled library.

Failures are R conditions classed c(<specific>, "zucrypt_error", "error", "condition"), mapped from the C status by enumerator name rather than by number. Every condition carries algorithm and native_status fields; for AES, algorithm names the cipher ("aes-256-cbc"), or "aes-cbc" when the key is what is wrong. No message ever contains a key, an IV or plaintext.

Fixed before the tag, from the package review in #51:

  • A condition no longer carries the call that raised it, only the function’s name. Before, print() on an error and conditionCall() showed the caller’s expression – literal keys and plaintext included – although the message itself was clean.
  • crypt_hmac() (and zuc_hmac_*()) accept keys of any length, as documented. Keys of 8,192 bytes or more used to fail with zucrypt_unsupported_algorithm, because the backend caps an imported key there; a key longer than the hash’s block is now hashed first, as RFC 2104 specifies, which gives the same MAC.
  • ?crypt_aes_cbc_nopad now authenticates the IV as well as the ciphertext in its encrypt-then-MAC advice and example. A MAC over the ciphertext alone let the IV, and so the first plaintext block, be changed undetected.

Renamed before release (#56): the CBC pair was crypt_aes_cbc_encrypt() and crypt_aes_cbc_decrypt() during development. The _nopad suffix names the difference from openssl::aes_cbc_encrypt(), which pads, so that code moved from openssl by changing a prefix can never silently get the padding back as plaintext. The unsuffixed names are reserved for an openssl-compatible padded pair. The C interface (zuc_aes_*()) is unchanged.

C interface

Both shapes the zu* family consumes siblings by, at ZUCRYPT_ABI_VERSION 1, with different stability (?zucrypt_c_api):

  • A static archive, libzucrypt.a, installed to lib/ plus the R sub-architecture (lib/x64/ on Windows), for a package that cannot carry an Imports: — LinkingTo: only, no runtime dependency, and the consumer owns the backend’s lifetime through zuc_init()/zuc_shutdown(). This is the primary shape, and it is frozen as ABI 1: within major version 1, functions may be added, nothing is removed or given a new meaning, and enumerator values are permanent.
  • A registered function table, inst/include/zucrypt-r.h, for a package that can carry an Imports:. Resolved lazily through zucrypt_api(); test an appended field with ZUCRYPT_API_HAS(). Experimental until a package uses it.

Settled before the freeze, from the first consumer’s report (#43):

  • zuc_alg values are grouped into reserved ranges, published as ZUC_ALG_*_FIRST/_LAST (digests, other MACs, ciphers and AEAD, key derivation, key families, signatures), so later families never renumber.
  • A buffer pointer may be NULL exactly when its length is 0, for the incremental digest and HMAC calls as for CBC – now stated, and tested.
  • The lifecycle note in zucrypt.h says what an R package needs for zuc_shutdown() to run at all: an .onUnload() that calls library.dynam.unload(). The archive fixture now does, and its checks prove the DLL is released.

inst/include/zucrypt.h compiles standalone as C99 against <stddef.h> and <stdint.h>, and names no backend type: a consumer never has to reproduce this package’s build configuration.

Both shapes are exercised on Linux, macOS and Windows by consumer fixture packages, as a real consumer would use them: - the table through an Imports: + LinkingTo: package that calls every entry; - the archive through a LinkingTo-only package whose configure resolves libzucrypt.a.

The archive fixture’s checks cover: - linking through a library path that contains a space; - exporting no backend symbol from its own shared object; - running beside zucrypt in the same R session, in either load order; - running with zucrypt not installed at all.

Settled before any consumer linked the ABI (design revision 3):

  • AES-ECB is not provided. Its one use was Office Standard encryption, which zuxlsx does not implement.
  • The backend’s key store grows on demand, so the number of live AES and HMAC handles is bounded only by memory. The static store it replaces allowed 16 live AES handles per process and reported the 17th as an allocation failure.
  • ZUC_ERR_NOT_READY (9) is returned by a call made before zuc_init() or after the last zuc_shutdown().
  • zuc_info gains hardware_acceleration, appended after the required prefix, and crypt_info()$build_flags$hardware_acceleration now reads it from the compiled library.
  • TF-PSA-Crypto’s licence is installed as licenses/tf-psa-crypto-LICENSE, since the archive carries its object code into every consumer.

Backend

Vendored TF-PSA-Crypto 1.1.1, an LTS release, trimmed to 113 files — the dependency closure of the sources that carry a symbol under this package’s configuration. Installation needs a C99 compiler and nothing else: no system cryptographic library, no CMake, no Python or Perl, and no network access.

AES runs on the CPU’s AES instructions — AES-NI on x86, the Cryptography Extension on 64-bit Arm — chosen at run time, and on a software fallback where the CPU has neither. The backend’s own security policy warns that the software fallback leaks key material through cache timing; crypt_info()$build_flags$aes_implementation reports which path a machine uses, and ?crypt_aes_cbc_nopad explains when that matters. Every path produces the same bytes. (Until the review in #51 hardware AES was off everywhere.)

Upstream symbols are hidden. The installed shared object exports exactly one symbol, R_init_zucrypt, so an independently vendored copy of the same library in another package cannot bind to this one, and no OpenSSL-ABI name is exported beside the libcrypto other packages link.

Supported platforms

Checked on every push: Linux, macOS (ARM64) and Windows; R release, oldrel-1 and 4.1; CRAN’s clang-23 and GCC-16 containers; the no-Suggests flavour; LTO; rchk and gctorture; ASan, UBSan, valgrind and GCC’s -fanalyzer. Weekly: i386, musl and aarch64 builds that run the test suite and fail on a WARNING, and a sweep that fails each allocation the crypt_*() calls make, one run per allocation — about 250 of them, of which some 77 land in zucrypt’s own code — checking that each surfaces as an error rather than a crash or a wrong answer.

Correctness is checked against published vectors — FIPS 180-2, RFC 2202, RFC 4231, RFC 6234 and NIST SP 800-38A, including the one-million-byte messages and HMAC keys longer than the block — every one of which is also recomputed with OpenSSL, an implementation sharing no code with the vendored backend. Inputs up to 4 MiB are compared with OpenSSL directly, and the iterated hash Office agile encryption uses is checked against msoffcrypto-tool.

Not in this release

Deliberate omissions, each waiting on a concrete consumer rather than on effort: authenticated encryption, password-based key derivation (PBKDF2, HKDF, Argon2), random byte generation, signatures, key serialization, file hashing and connection wrappers. There is no encrypt_file(password = ), and there will not be one without a specified authenticated format, a nonce policy and a key derivation step.

Office/Excel decryption is not here either. It belongs to zuxlsx, which consumes this package.
